learning_outcomes.text: Understand complex concepts of classical and AI-based image processing, including image representation, image segmentation, and object recognition, and apply these techniques effectively in various application areas.

Deepen the fundamentals of image processing and AI architectures, understanding complex concepts such as image representation, classification, and object recognition. Analyze and apply these techniques to practical use cases, effectively applying knowledge in various real-world scenarios.

Transfer CV concepts into practical applications. Analyze and apply algorithms to various scenarios, determining when classical CV and AI-based approaches are best suited and implementing them in real environments.

syllabus_topics: Image representation and storage / AI datasets for CV
Real-time CV - vectorized algorithms & GPU applications
Privacy and data protection vs. CV - using CV correctly
assessment_rules: The graded assessment is either a written project report (10 pages plus a 15-minute presentation) or an oral project report (30-minute presentation). An ungraded experimental work consisting of 6 worksheets is also required.
bibliography: Dawson-Howe, Kenneth. A practical introduction to computer vision with opencv. John Wiley & Sons, 2014.
Kaehler, Adrian, and Gary Bradski. Learning OpenCV 3: computer vision in C++ with the OpenCV library. " O'Reilly Media, Inc.", 2016.
Dadhich, Abhinav. Practical Computer Vision: Extract Insightful Information from Images Using TensorFlow, Keras, and OpenCV. Packt Publishing Ltd, 2018.
Géron, Aurélien. Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow: Concepts, Tools, and Techniques to Build Intelligent Systems. O'Reilly Media, 2019.
